## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/02.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">2021 Data Reporting and Use
 • Recent federal guidance indicates that states are responsible to
 report results from 2021 testing (however not used for
 accountability)
 • State reporting is, in general, highly aligned with accountability.
 • Even though analyses outlined herein deal with status/growth, they
 don’t necessarily align with accountability narratives.
 • It is critical for leadership (at the highest level) to map out a
 communication plan and then build analytics and reporting to
 support that plan.
 • Without a well considered, disciplined and coordinated
 communication plan, accountability narratives are likely to take over.
 ID TAC COVID-19 Academic Impact Discussion</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">COVID-19 Pandemic
 • Now a year into the pandemic, there is strong evidence
 that the pandemic is having a negative impact on children
 nationwide.
 • Negative impacts extend beyond academic impact and
 include financial, social-emotional and physical impact.

 ID TAC COVID-19 Academic Impact Discussion</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">COVID-19 Pandemic: Academic Impact
 • Academic impact of the pandemic is often referred to variously
 as learning loss, unfinished learning, COVID-19 slide.
 • As states formulate policies to help with student academic
 recovery, there is a need for data/information/evidence on:
 • Who: Who is experiencing or has experienced learning loss?
 • What: What have students experienced learning loss in?
 • How Much: How much learning loss have students experienced?
 • Answers to these questions will be critical in helping to
 understand how to help? For example, if learning loss is
 substantial for some groups, recovery will not be immediate
 and will require many months if not years to ameliorate.

 ID TAC COVID-19 Academic Impact Discussion</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/05.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">COVID-19 Pandemic: Data
 • Data are necessary to answer Who?, What? and How much?
 • Idaho has extensive academic data available to determine
 learning loss for students:
 • ISAT state summative assessment data
 • WIDA-ACCESS English Language Proficiency data (ELL students)
 • Interim assessment data from assessment vendors.
 • Multiple sources of data allow for:
 • Investigation of student groups not contained in some data sets (e.g.,
 ELL students)
 • Triangulation of results across multiple data sets.
 ID TAC COVID-19 Academic Impact Discussion</div>
```

 • Operational analyses (not discussed here) are necessary to insure the validity of these data

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/07.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">COVID-19 Pandemic: Conceptualizing
Academic Impact
 • Think of the pandemic as a head-wind that slowed the progress of students.
 • As such, there are two ways to use data to detect the impact of the
 pandemic.
 • Status change: Compare similar grade/content area groups from 2019 to 2021.
 Need to take special care the groups are comparable.
 • Growth change: Compare growth rates for students from 2019 to 2021 using
 historical norms.
 • Both status and growth comparisons get at the same thing --- the impact of
 the pandemic on student attainment.
 • NOTE: Any analysis of pandemic impact (status or growth) requires
 comparison to a counterfactual baseline!
 • NOTE: If you provide 2021 results (status or growth), stakeholder will (rightly)
 want to compare that to pre-COVID (e.g., 2019) results.

 ID TAC COVID-19 Academic Impact Discussion</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/09.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">COVID-19 Pandemic: Academic Recovery
 • With some understanding of the academic impact of the
 pandemic the next step is plan for and monitor recovery.
 • The magnitude of the impact (how much?) will indicate the
 magnitude of the recovery.
 • Early evidence from interim assessments suggest that in
 elementary school mathematics, students in some states have lost
 more than 12 weeks of learning.
 • Learning loss in ELA is more modest for these interim assessments.
 • Learning recovery will take on many forms (V-, U-, L-shaped
 recoveries)
 ID TAC COVID-19 Academic Impact Discussion</div>
```
